findings.claim: The grader half of R2 is refused on a false premise: T-R85's stated treadmill-free check passes the very defect it claims would have been caught, so ADR-019 §3's pointer at it overstates the coverage that debt item would buy.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:1594 — 'Grade published >= max(wall_s of rows at this count with ts <= the cited ts)', justified at tasks/reviews/pr45-r1-resolution.json (rejected_scope) by 'it would have caught this exact defect: 002424 was cited when 002326/14.02 already stood'. Arithmetic on the committed ledger: rows at invariant/59 with ts <= 20260824-002424 are 14.02 and 14.08, max 14.08; the defective publication was 14.08, so 14.08 >= 14.08 is GREEN. The R2 defect was citing 002424 when the slower 003025/14.16 stood at a LATER ts, which an as-of-the-cited-ts bound cannot see by construction — an author can always satisfy it by citing an early row, which is precisely what happened. ADR-019:145-147 sends the reader to T-R85 as 'the treadmill-free form of the check' for a class it would not catch.
findings.repro: git show 32cb549:evals/report/history.jsonl piped through the as-of-max computation for cited 002424/published 14.08 and cited 003025/published 14.16 -> both True (both green).
